† I. [נָקַף] vb. strike off (NH strike, wound, Aramaic נְקַף id.; Arabic نَقَفَ fregit caput, ut cerebrum appareret; Vulg. Ar. snap with the finger (Dozyii, 716); Assyrian naḳpu prob. = mutilated; Ethiopic ነቀፈ peel, flay Di649);—
Niph. Pf. 3 ms. וְנִקַּף סִבְכֵי הַיַּ֫עַר consec. Is 10:34 and the thickets of the forest shall be struck away (on sg. vb. cf. Ges§ 145 o DaSynt. § 113 b; or read נִקְּפוּ;—form poss. Pi., but cf. Di Du CheHpt).
Pi. Pf. 3 pl. וְאַחַר עוֹרִי נִקְּפוּ־זֹאת Jb 19:26 after my skin, which they (Ges§ 144 g) have struck off (alluding to ravages of his disease)—this! but text dub.; Bu נִקַּף כָּזֹאת (Niph.) which has been thus struck off.
